steps.tx: Drug-induced **acute interstitial nephritis**, abbreviated as **AIN**, is an immune-mediated hypersensitivity reaction triggered most frequently by **proton pump inhibitors**, beta-lactam antibiotics, fluoroquinolones, sulfonamides, and **NSAIDs**, causing acute renal functional decline. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring. Careful ongoing monitoring ensures optimal patient outcomes and prevents secondary complications.

steps.tx: The classical **allergic triad** of fever, maculopapular rash, and peripheral **eosinophilia** is present in fewer than **10%** of patients with drug-induced **AIN**. Because clinical signs are frequently subtle, definitive diagnosis requires confirmation by percutaneous **kidney biopsy**. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

steps.tx: Histopathological examination in acute interstitial nephritis demonstrates prominent **interstitial edema**, dense infiltration by lymphocytes and macrophages, interspersed **eosinophils**, and active **tubulitis** characterized by inflammatory cells crossing tubular basement membranes. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring. Careful ongoing monitoring ensures optimal patient outcomes and prevents secondary complications.

left.title: Acute Phase (AIN)
points: Tubular injury: Active tubulitis with basement membrane crossing
Reversibility: Highly reversible with prompt therapy

right.title: Chronic Phase (CIN)
points: Tubular injury: Widespread tubular atrophy and thyroidization

steps.tx: Early oral **corticosteroid** therapy with **prednisone** at **1** mg/kg/day for **2** to **3** weeks followed by a **4**- to **6**-week taper, initiated within **7** to **14** days of offending drug cessation, significantly accelerates renal recovery and suppresses irreversible **interstitial fibrosis**. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.
steps.say: Early oral corticosteroid therapy with prednisone at 1 mg/kg/day for 2 to 3 weeks followed by a 4- to 6-week taper, initiated within 7 to 14 days of offending drug cessation, significantly accelerates renal recovery and suppresses irreversible interstitial fibrosis. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

nodes.label: Taper over 4 to 6 weeks to prevent fibrosis

steps.tx: **NSAID-induced** interstitial nephritis characteristically combines interstitial inflammatory infiltration with heavy **nephrotic-range proteinuria**. Renal biopsy reveals marked podocyte foot process effacement identical to **minimal change** disease, mediated by cyclooxygenase inhibition shunting arachidonate to leukotrienes. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

left.title: Standard Drug AIN (PPI / Antibiotics)
points: Proteinuria level: Sub-nephrotic tubular proteinuria < 1 g/day
Glomerular structure: Completely normal podocyte foot processes
Allergic features: Eosinophils and mild systemic signs
Renal recovery: Rapid upon drug withdrawal and steroids

right.title: NSAID-Induced AIN
points: Proteinuria level: Heavy nephrotic-range proteinuria > 3.5 g/day
Glomerular structure: Diffuse podocyte foot process effacement
Pathophysiology: Dual interstitial nephritis and minimal change lesion
Renal recovery: Prolonged recovery requiring extended steroid taper

steps.tx: **IgG4-related** tubulointerstitial nephritis presents with dense plasma cell infiltration containing greater than **10** **IgG4-positive plasma cells** per high-power field, characteristic **storiform fibrosis**, and elevated serum IgG4, frequently accompanied by autoimmune pancreatitis. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.
steps.say: IgG4-related tubulointerstitial nephritis presents with dense plasma cell infiltration containing greater than 10 IgG4-positive plasma cells per high-power field, characteristic storiform fibrosis, and elevated serum IgG4, frequently accompanied by autoimmune pancreatitis. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

rows: Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with > 10 IgG4+ cells/HPF
Can progress to irreversible renal atrophy if untreated
Elevated serum IgG4 and bilateral swollen kidneys
Normalizes in parallel with disease remission

steps.tx: **Tubulointerstitial nephritis and uveitis**, designated as **TINU syndrome**, predominantly affects adolescent females. Patients present with acute interstitial nephritis, elevated urinary **beta-2 microglobulin**, and painful bilateral **anterior uveitis**, responding favorably to systemic corticosteroids. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Balkan endemic nephropathy** and Chinese herb nephropathy are caused by chronic ingestion of **aristolochic acid**. Biopsy shows extensive **hypocellular interstitial fibrosis** and marked urothelial atypia, carrying an extraordinarily high risk of **upper tract urothelial carcinoma**. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.
